mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous and PAYEMS > previous in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day log returns of SPX are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the triggered period.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of retail sales (not available in the provided catalog) to GDP growth turns positive, it indicates pent-up demand that accelerates corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. candidate_trigger: GDPC1 / INDPRO > 1 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to exceed baseline by at least 0.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level indicates cyclical bottoming, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO shows a double-bottom pattern over a 4-quarter window
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (p > 0.05) during the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3% for three consecutive months, it suggests central banks are less likely to raise rates, preserving discount rate stability and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in job openings (not available) suggests labor market weakness that dampens consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the triggered period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail activity ( proxy: GDPC1 ) and stable housing starts (not available) create momentum in consumer confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days when both series show upward trends.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat with no upward deviation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4%) and rising real rates (FEDFUNDS), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative due to discounting future cash flows at higher rates, even if equity price momentum is positive.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0 for the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when conditions are met.
